title: Telling what happened
job: A four-sentence account in the past
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: TWO PASTS, TWO JOBS. The imperfetto paints the standing situation a story happens against — what was already going on, what things were like, the weather, a habit, an age. The passato prossimo moves the account forward one completed step at a time. Era tardi e non c'era nessuno. Allora ho chiamato Anna. L1-M5 shipped the second one and never taught the choice; this is where it is taught.

THE SLOGAN TO KILL: "one tense is for completed actions and the other for ongoing ones". It breaks on the first real account. Ieri ho mangiato alle sette is completed. Mangiavo quando hai chiamato is not "ongoing" in any objective sense — it is background for the call. Da bambino andavo sempre al mare is a habit, not a duration. What decides it is the ROLE the clause plays in the telling.

THE AUXILIARY LAW, written down at last: essere for movement and change of state — è andato, sono partiti, siamo tornati — and for reflexives, with the participle agreeing with the SUBJECT in gender and number. avere for everything else, with no agreement at all. L1 taught the agreement by example (sono andata, siamo andati); here is the rule behind it.

The sequencers are the honest new spend: prima, dopo and alla fine, joining L1-M10's poi and allora. Each account is four short sentences rather than one long one, and almost every word in them comes from L1 and from M1–M9.

Nothing new is opened. The passato remoto, the trapassato, the congiuntivo and reported speech all stay OUT and belong to L3 — which is why an account here reports what happened and never what anyone said about it.

sentences.display: Era tardi. Non c'era nessuno. Allora ho chiamato Anna
sentences.cue: It was late. There was nobody. So I called Anna
sentences.literal: Was late. Not there-was nobody. Then I-have called Anna

words.note: The standing situation, not a step. Era tardi says what things were like; it does not move the story on.
L1-M7's c'è in the imperfetto, and an elision, so ONE index key. Its plural is c'erano, for more than one thing.
It needs the non in front of the verb: non c'era nessuno. Italian doubles its negatives where English forbids it, and dropping the non is the error.
The participle of chiamare, which L1-M1 met inside mi chiamo. With avere it does not agree — that is the easy half of the auxiliary law.

sentences.trap: Two imperfetti set the scene and one passato prossimo moves it. That is the whole architecture of an Italian account, and it is visible in three short sentences.
sentences.sound: E-ra TAR-dee. non CHE-ra nes-SOO-no. c'era is two syllables with the elision joining them.

variations.display: Era tardi. Allora ho chiamato Anna
variations.cue: It was late. So I called Anna
variations.changed: two steps instead of three

variations.display: Era presto. Non c'era nessuno
variations.cue: It was early. There was nobody
variations.changed: a different situation

variations.display: Non c'era nessuno. Allora sono tornato a casa
variations.cue: There was nobody. So I went back home
variations.changed: movement, so essere and an agreeing participle

mistake.display: Era tardi. C'era nessuno. Allora ho chiamato Anna
mistake.why: The negative needs its non: Non c'era nessuno.

sentences.usage: Opening an account — the situation first, then what you did about it.
sentences.mnemonic: Imperfetto sets the scene. Passato prossimo moves it.

sentences.cue: I was eating when you called

words.note: The imperfetto of L1-M3's mangiare. It is the background the call interrupted — and it is not "ongoing" in any objective sense, just the frame.
It glues the two tenses together: background before it, event after it. It also asks a question — Quando sei tornato? — and the word is the same.
The imperfetto of L1-M1's lavorare. Every -are verb takes the same -avo, -avi, -ava endings, so the class is regular throughout.

sentences.trap: The eating and the call took the same kind of time. What separates them is that one is scenery and the other is the event, which is a decision about the telling rather than about the world.
sentences.sound: man-JA-vo KWAN-do ai kya-MA-to. The -avo ending is where every -are imperfetto lands.

variations.display: Lavoravo quando hai chiamato
variations.cue: I was working when you called
variations.changed: a different background

variations.display: Mangiavo quando è tornato
variations.cue: I was eating when he got back
variations.changed: a return, so essere and agreement

variations.display: Ieri ho mangiato alle sette
variations.cue: Yesterday I ate at seven
variations.changed: a completed step — the same verb, the other tense

mistake.why: The background clause is imperfetto: Mangiavo quando hai chiamato.

sentences.usage: Explaining what you were in the middle of.

sentences.display: Ieri pioveva. Sono rimasto a casa
sentences.cue: Yesterday it was raining. I stayed at home
sentences.literal: Yesterday it-was-raining. I-am stayed at home

words.note: The imperfetto of L1-M9's piove. Weather is almost always imperfetto in an account, because it is the scenery rather than an event.
An irregular participle, and it takes essere because staying put is a change of state in Italian's reckoning. So it agrees with the subject.

sentences.trap: rimanere takes essere even though nothing moves. The law is "movement and change of state", and Italian counts staying as the second — which is a place the rule has to be learnt rather than reasoned out.
sentences.sound: pyo-VE-va. SO-no ree-MA-sto. The io of pioveva is one glide.

variations.display: Ieri pioveva. Sono rimasta a casa
variations.cue: Yesterday it was raining. I stayed at home
variations.changed: said by a woman, so the participle agrees

variations.display: Faceva freddo. Sono rimasto a casa
variations.cue: It was cold. I stayed at home
variations.changed: a different kind of weather

variations.display: Ieri pioveva. Ho preso l'autobus
variations.cue: Yesterday it was raining. I took the bus
variations.changed: avere, and no agreement at all

mistake.display: Ieri pioveva. Ho rimasto a casa
mistake.why: rimanere takes essere: Sono rimasto a casa.

sentences.usage: Explaining a day that did not go to plan.

sentences.display: Faceva freddo e non avevo la chiave
sentences.cue: It was cold and I didn't have my key
sentences.literal: It-was-making cold and not I-had the key

words.note: Italian MAKES weather rather than being it: fa freddo, faceva caldo. L1-M6's fare in the imperfetto, doing the job English gives to "is".
The imperfetto of avere. Having something is a state rather than an event, so it is nearly always this tense in an account.

sentences.trap: Both halves are imperfetto because neither is a step. Nothing has happened yet in this sentence — it is entirely scene-setting, and the account has not started to move.
sentences.sound: fa-CHE-va FRED-do. The ce is a soft ch, and the double d is held.

variations.display: Faceva caldo e non avevo acqua
variations.cue: It was hot and I had no water
variations.changed: the opposite weather

variations.display: Faceva freddo. Sono tornato a casa
variations.cue: It was cold. I went back home
variations.changed: with a step after the scene

variations.display: Non avevo la chiave
variations.cue: I didn't have my key
variations.changed: the second half alone

mistake.display: Era freddo e non avevo la chiave
mistake.why: Weather is made, not been: Faceva freddo.

sentences.usage: Setting up a story that is about to go wrong.

sentences.display: Prima ho mangiato, poi sono uscito
sentences.cue: First I ate, then I went out
sentences.literal: Before I-have eaten, then I-am gone-out

words.note: As an adverb it does not agree — M4's prima strada was the adjective, and this is the other job the word does.
L1-M6's uscire, and movement, so essere and agreement. A woman says sono uscita.

sentences.trap: One sentence, two auxiliaries: ho with mangiare and sono with uscire. Nothing about the meaning of the two events differs — only whether the verb involves movement.
sentences.sound: PREE-ma o man-JA-to poi SO-no oo-SHEE-to. The sci of uscito is a soft sh.

variations.display: Prima ho mangiato, poi sono uscita
variations.cue: First I ate, then I went out
variations.changed: said by a woman

variations.display: Prima sono uscito, poi ho mangiato
variations.cue: First I went out, then I ate
variations.changed: the order swapped, and the auxiliaries with it

variations.display: Ho mangiato e poi sono uscito
variations.cue: I ate and then went out
variations.changed: joined with e rather than split

mistake.display: Prima ho mangiato, poi ho uscito
mistake.why: Movement takes essere: poi sono uscito.

sentences.usage: Telling someone the order things happened in.

sentences.display: Ho perso il treno. Alla fine ho preso l'autobus
sentences.cue: I missed the train. In the end I took the bus
sentences.literal: I-have lost the train. At-the end I-have taken the-bus

words.note: Two words, closing an account. It marks the last step rather than merely the latest one.
The irregular participle of L1-M6's prendere. Its forms exist, but after avere none of them is ever used — the cells are there for the essere verbs to borrow.

sentences.trap: Both verbs take avere and neither participle agrees. That is the easy half of the law — with avere nothing on the end ever moves.
sentences.sound: AL-la FEE-ne. The double l is held, and both words are stressed on the first syllable.

variations.display: Ho perso il treno. Alla fine sono tornato a casa
variations.cue: I missed the train. In the end I went back home
variations.changed: movement in the second half, so essere

variations.display: Alla fine ho preso l'autobus
variations.cue: In the end I took the bus
variations.changed: the second half alone

variations.display: Ho perso il treno. Poi ho preso l'autobus
variations.cue: I missed the train. Then I took the bus
variations.changed: poi rather than alla fine — a step, not the last one

mistake.display: Ho perso il treno. Alla fine ho presa l'autobus
mistake.why: With avere the participle does not agree: ho preso l'autobus.

sentences.usage: The story of a journey that went wrong and then worked out.

sentences.display: C'era molta gente. Dopo siamo tornati a casa
sentences.cue: There were a lot of people. Afterwards we went home
sentences.literal: There-was much people. After we-are returned to home

words.note: SINGULAR in Italian — molta gente, c'era gente — where English is plural. The verb and the adjective both follow the Italian number, not the English one.
M4's dopo doing a second job: there it was a place preposition, here it is a sequencer standing alone.
The noi cell of essere, and here it is the auxiliary. L1-M10 showed siamo andati without ever opening the word itself.
L1-M10's tornato and tornata in the plural. Movement takes essere, so the participle counts and genders the people who came back.

sentences.trap: gente is singular, so it is c'era and molta and not c'erano and molte. Translating the English plural gets three words wrong at once.
sentences.sound: JEN-te. The ge is soft, and the word is two syllables.

variations.display: C'era molta gente. Dopo sono tornato a casa
variations.cue: There were a lot of people. Afterwards I went home
variations.changed: one person, so the participle agrees with him

variations.display: Non c'era molta gente
variations.cue: There weren't many people
variations.changed: negated

variations.display: C'era molta gente. Alla fine siamo tornati a casa
variations.cue: There were a lot of people. In the end we went home
variations.changed: the closing sequencer

mistake.display: C'erano molte gente. Dopo siamo tornati a casa
mistake.why: gente is singular: C'era molta gente.

sentences.usage: Describing a place that was crowded, and what you did about it.

sentences.display: Da bambino andavo sempre al mare
sentences.cue: As a child I always went to the seaside
sentences.literal: From child I-was-going always to-the sea

words.note: A habit, so the imperfetto — and a habit is not a duration. English needs "used to" here, and Italian needs only the tense.
Al mare means the seaside as a place to go. It is masculine, and an -e noun, so its plural is in -i.
One whole thing, with no article inside it. da here means "in the state of", which is a job it does in a handful of fixed phrases.

sentences.trap: Nothing here is ongoing and nothing is background. It is a habit, which is the third job the imperfetto does — and the one that most clearly breaks the "ongoing" slogan.
sentences.sound: da bam-BEE-no an-DA-vo. Da bambino has no article, which is what makes it "as a child".

variations.display: Da bambina andavo sempre al mare
variations.cue: As a child I always went to the seaside
variations.changed: said by a woman

variations.display: Da bambino mangiavo sempre a casa
variations.cue: As a child I always ate at home
variations.changed: a different habit

variations.display: Andavo sempre al mare
variations.cue: I always used to go to the seaside
variations.changed: without saying when

mistake.display: Da bambino sono andato sempre al mare
mistake.why: A habit takes the imperfetto: Da bambino andavo sempre al mare.

sentences.usage: Talking about childhood, which is where the imperfetto lives.
sentences.mnemonic: A habit is not a duration.

sentences.display: Era tardi. Ho chiamato Anna. Alla fine siamo usciti
sentences.cue: It was late. I called Anna. In the end we went out
sentences.literal: Was late. I-have called Anna. At-the end we-are gone-out

words.note: The tu cell of the imperfetto of essere, beside ero and era. Dov'eri? is "where were you?" and is what an account often opens with.
dove plus eri, elided into ONE key — the same fusion as L1-M7's dov'è. It is the question an account is usually an answer to.

sentences.trap: Three sentences, one scene and two steps. The scene is imperfetto and both steps are passato prossimo — and the second one takes essere because going out is movement.
sentences.sound: E-ra TAR-dee. o kya-MA-to AN-na. AL-la FEE-ne SYA-mo oo-SHEE-tee. Three short sentences and three clear beats.

variations.display: Era tardi. Ho chiamato Anna
variations.cue: It was late. I called Anna
variations.changed: two sentences instead of three

variations.display: Ero stanco. Alla fine sono tornato a casa
variations.cue: I was tired. In the end I went home
variations.changed: a different scene and a different ending

variations.display: Dov'eri ieri?
variations.cue: Where were you yesterday?
variations.changed: the question that asks for an account

mistake.display: Era tardi. Ho chiamato Anna. Alla fine abbiamo usciti
mistake.why: Movement takes essere: Alla fine siamo usciti.

sentences.usage: A whole small account — a situation, a step, an outcome.

sentences.display: Ieri faceva caldo. Siamo andati al mare. Alla fine ho dormito
sentences.cue: Yesterday it was hot. We went to the seaside. In the end I slept
sentences.literal: Yesterday it-was-making hot. We-are gone to-the sea. At-the end I-have slept

words.note: The io cell of the imperfetto of essere. Ero stanco, ero a casa — a state, never a step.
The third-person cell of avevo. The whole imperfetto of avere is regular, unlike its present.

sentences.trap: Three verbs, three different auxiliaries or tenses, and each one is chosen by the rule rather than by the meaning: weather is scenery, going is movement, sleeping is neither.
sentences.sound: fa-CHE-va KAL-do. SYA-mo an-DA-tee al MA-re. The participle andati agrees with a plural we.

variations.display: Ieri faceva caldo. Siamo andati al mare
variations.cue: Yesterday it was hot. We went to the seaside
variations.changed: two sentences

variations.display: Faceva caldo. Sono andato al mare
variations.cue: It was hot. I went to the seaside
variations.changed: one person, so the participle agrees with him

variations.display: Ero stanco. Alla fine ho dormito
variations.cue: I was tired. In the end I slept
variations.changed: a different scene, and avere on the last verb

mistake.display: Ieri faceva caldo. Abbiamo andati al mare. Alla fine ho dormito
mistake.why: Movement takes essere: Siamo andati al mare.

sentences.usage: A whole day told in three sentences, which is what an account is.
sentences.mnemonic: The rule picks the auxiliary, not the meaning.
